source.title: Deep neural networks are biased towards simple functions
source.authors: Giacomo De Palma; B. Kiani; S. Lloyd

record.file_problem: Text is the full paper, though some PDF text and figure labels are garbled. Table 1 is referenced as Table ?? in the body; its contents appear later.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures classification-boundary distance in trained networks and reports its association with classification accuracy, a different measure and outcome from the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's results on random untrained networks and trained MNIST networks concern boundary distance and sensitivity to input changes. It does not test memorization of random labels, training-versus-test error gaps, the listed interventions, or magnitude-aware sharpness. Prior-work findings are cited but are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures input robustness and classification-boundary distance, not any of V1–V8. Input perturbations are distinct from V7's magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, and correctness of individual examples is distinct from ranking training–test gaps. The reported 98.8% MNIST test accuracy alone does not test any version's comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors prove an input-insensitivity bias for random wide ReLU networks and report that substantial boundary distances persist in their MNIST experiments. They interpret the association between boundary distance and correctness as relevant to generalization; they do not demonstrate a relationship with measured training–test gaps.
record.recipe_differences: Studies simplicity and classification-boundary distances in randomly initialized networks, plus a trained MNIST even-or-odd experiment; it does not reproduce the claim's memorization or generalization-gap comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different boundary-distance behavior for random bit strings versus training and test pictures; distances also differ between correctly and incorrectly classified pictures.

fits_no_version.finding: Untrained random ReLU networks have nearest-boundary distances scaling approximately as sqrt(n/(2π ln n)); random nonrepeating bit flips require approximately 0.33n steps to change classification.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random wide ReLU networks favor binary functions whose classifications tolerate substantial absolute changes in their inputs.

fits_no_version.finding: In trained MNIST networks, random inputs have average nearest-boundary distance close to 4.33, while training and test images have larger average distances.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested MNIST networks tolerate more input-bit changes around data examples than around random binary inputs.

fits_no_version.finding: Correctly classified images have larger average boundary distances than incorrectly classified images: 10.61 versus 1.42 for training and 10.47 versus 2.30 for test.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-boundary distance is associated with per-example classification correctness in the tested MNIST even-or-odd networks.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2019, as stated in the paper header
record.problems: The MNIST analysis uses a specific binary even-or-odd task and fully connected networks. Boundary distance is estimated with a greedy search. The paper does not report uncertainty intervals for these results, and the text does not quantify the train/test generalization gap.
record.rows_left_out: No results bearing on the listed versions were reported. Cited results from prior work were excluded. Figure 3b's slopes and figure-only distributions were not extracted as they are boundary-distance relationships without values needed for the listed versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label performance under the same recipe, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, training–test gap rankings, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; the unrelated boundary-distance findings themselves are reported effects. No listed-version results require additional rows.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence; random-label held-out chance accuracy.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and training-test gap ranking.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test-accuracy effects.

rows.subject: randomly generated neural networks
rows.size_stated: two fully connected hidden layers, each with n neurons; input size varies
rows.operation_detail: Greedy search for Hamming distance from a random bit string to the nearest differently classified string

conditions.value: greedy; exact search also compared for smaller networks

rows.measure: Average Hamming distance to nearest differently classified bit string
rows.value: scales as n/(2π ln n); pre-factor 1/√(2π) confirmed with precision of 1.5%
rows.note: Results concern untrained random networks and input-boundary distance, not natural-label training or test error.
rows.check: The value omits a square root: the scaling is sqrt(n/(2π ln n)), with fitted coefficient 0.405 multiplying sqrt(n/ln n). These are input-boundary distances in untrained networks and cannot establish a listed version.

rows.subject: randomly generated neural networks
rows.size_stated: two fully connected hidden layers, each with n neurons; input size varies
rows.operation_detail: Measured steps in a random sequence of bit flips until classification changed
rows.measure: Average Hamming distance to differently classified bit string
rows.value: scales linearly with input size; simulated pre-factor 0.33, versus heuristic lower bound 0.25
rows.note: A robustness/sensitivity result for untrained networks, not a training-test error result.
rows.check: The reported scaling and approximate coefficients are correct, but measure input robustness rather than a listed effect. Each bit is flipped at most once; 0.25 is a heuristic estimate, not the quantitative bound proved by Theorem 2.

rows.subject: 2-layer fully-connected neural networks
rows.size_stated: two fully connected hidden layers, each with 784 neurons; 784 binary inputs
rows.operation_detail: Trained to classify MNIST digits as even or odd; measured boundary distance for random bit strings

conditions.value: random bit strings, each bit equally likely 0 or 1

rows.measure: Average minimum Hamming distance to a differently classified string
rows.value: close to the expected theoretical value of approximately 4.33
rows.note: The text reports this comparison, but does not give a separate empirical numeric average.
rows.check: The approximately 4.33 theoretical expectation and qualitative empirical agreement are supported. Random input strings are not random training labels, and this measure cannot establish any listed version.

rows.subject: 2-layer fully-connected neural networks
rows.size_stated: two fully connected hidden layers, each with 784 neurons; 784 binary inputs
rows.operation_detail: Compared boundary distances for correctly and incorrectly classified training examples
rows.measure: Average distance to nearest classification boundary by classification correctness
rows.note: The authors report boundary distance as empirically correlated with classification accuracy and generalization properties.
rows.check: The distances 1.42 and 10.61 are correctly transcribed. Figure 4 specifies 20 networks trained for 10 epochs, whereas Section 4.3 describes 400 networks trained for 20 epochs; the row's definite 20-epoch attribution overlooks this discrepancy. Per-example correctness versus input-boundary distance does not measure V7.

rows.subject: 2-layer fully-connected neural networks
rows.size_stated: two fully connected hidden layers, each with 784 neurons; 784 binary inputs
rows.operation_detail: Compared boundary distances for correctly and incorrectly classified test examples
rows.measure: Average distance to nearest classification boundary by classification correctness
rows.note: The paper gives these averages and says boundary distance is empirically correlated with classification accuracy and generalization properties.
rows.check: The distances 2.30 and 10.47 are correctly transcribed. Figure 4 specifies 20 networks trained for 10 epochs, conflicting with the broader Section 4.3 description of 400 networks trained for 20 epochs. This association does not measure training–test gap rankings or weight sharpness.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
